cases.sentence: Народ ходил и собирал ее, а затем перемалывал ее ___ или толок в ступе.
cases.explain: «ручными жерновами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The people went around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.

cases.sentence: По вкусу она напоминала лепешки, испеченные с ___.
cases.explain: «оливковым маслом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The people went around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.

cases.sentence: Скажи народу: «Освятитесь к ___, и будете есть мясо.
cases.explain: «завтрашнему дню» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Say to the people, ‘Sanctify yourselves in preparation for tomorrow, and you will eat meat; for you have wept in the ears of Yahweh, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Egypt.” Therefore Yahweh will give you meat, and you will eat.

cases.sentence: Они были везде на расстоянии ___ в каждую сторону от лагеря, летая на высоте около двух локтей от земли.
cases.explain: «дневного пути» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A wind from Yahweh went out and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the earth.

cases.sentence: Весь тот день, всю ночь и весь ___ народ ходил собирать перепелов, и никто не собрал меньше десяти хомеров .
cases.explain: «следующий день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The people rose up all that day, and all of that night, and all the next day, and gathered the quails. He who gathered least gathered ten homers;  and they spread them all out for themselves around the camp.
